analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: Q3 2026 midseason earnings update
key_insights: With 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth is tracking at 33% y/y, matching Q2 (excluding non-recurring items). This ends the pattern of acceleration over the last few quarters. The 10-year median Q3 growth rate is 10%.

GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth of nearly 30% in 2026 to slow to 18% in 2027 excluding non-recurring items. The S&P 500 is on pace for a fourth straight year of double-digit returns despite a volatile macro backdrop and falling valuation multiples.

Median S&P 500 stock EPS growth is tracking at 12% y/y, above the 10-year median of 8% but down from 14% last quarter. Aggregate growth is carried by a few sectors: Info Tech and Communication Services together account for more than 60% of Q3 EPS growth and Energy adds another 20%.

Beat rate is above its long-run average but below recent quarters. 60% of companies beat consensus EPS by more than one standard deviation of analyst estimates, versus a 50% historical average and a 64% average over the past 4 quarters. The aggregate upside surprise is smaller than in Q1 and Q2.

The median stock beating EPS estimates outperformed the S&P 500 by about 152 bp on the day after reporting, above the historical median of 95 bp. This reverses several quarters of below-average rewards for beats. Cyclical sectors, which saw a large drop in hedge fund positioning, reacted best. TMT beats went unrewarded (TMT median -76 bp, non-TMT +172 bp).

Narrow breadth is partly resolving through a simultaneous catch up and catch down. Since the start of the season 70% of S&P 500 companies have posted positive returns but they account for only 50% of market cap. The index is down 3% while the S&P 500 ex. AI is up 5%. GS says the outlook for energy prices and interest rates will determine whether non-tech stocks keep rising.

Estimate revisions are positive but slowing. Consensus 2027 S&P 500 EPS is up 2% since the start of the season. Revision breadth is positive in only half of S&P 500 sectors, with Info Tech and Energy strongest. Analysts raised 2027 sales estimates but trimmed margin estimates for many companies as input costs and energy prices rise.

Hyperscaler capex is expected to be roughly $800B in 2026 (+96% y/y) and $1.2T in 2027 (+44%). Estimates barely moved this season, unlike the upward revisions of recent quarters. GS reads this as consistent with capex growth and upside surprises to consensus having peaked, while spending still rises substantially in 2027.

AI infrastructure stocks (hyperscalers, semiconductors, power companies and others in GS baskets) are on track for 80% aggregate EPS growth in Q3, more than 5 times the 15% growth of the rest of the S&P 500. Consensus has this slowing sharply to about 40% by late 2027.

Hyperscaler aggregate free cash flow (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT, ORCL) turned negative in Q3 2026 because capex now exceeds operating cash flow. Consensus shows free cash flow declining further in 2027 and turning positive again in 2028.

Cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT reached 54% y/y in Q3, up from 48% in Q2 and 39% in Q1. Cloud revenue beat consensus, but crowded hedge fund positioning ahead of the reports set a high bar for share prices. Cloud backlog growth decelerated slightly versus Q2.

Results renewed investor focus on AI disruption risk, especially in TMT. GS analysts flagged disappointing Alphabet search revenues and reduced search referral traffic to Reddit. GS economists noted early signs of AI-related labor market disruption.

Profit margins for the median S&P 500 stock expanded to a record high in Q3 while median revenue growth decelerated modestly. Industrials margins keep rising and Consumer Staples margins are struggling.

By sector, Q3 EPS growth is Energy 138% (margin +736 bp), Info Tech 67% (sales +43%, margin +454 bp), Communication Services 46%, Materials 39%, Industrials 23%, Consumer Discretionary 16%, Utilities 11%, Health Care 4%, Financials 4% and Consumer Staples 2%. S&P 500 ex. Financials and Utilities is 43%.

Biggest S&P 500 movers this week: Pentair, Vertiv, Carvana, Gen Digital and Global Payments led, each up 17-20%. ServiceNow (-34%), F5 (-26%), Fortinet (-24%), Intel (-24%) and Twilio (-22%) fell most. Communication Services fell 8.8% on the week and Media & Entertainment 9.1%.
Next week 143 companies representing 21% of S&P 500 market cap report Q3 results.

GS top-down S&P 500 forecasts: 7720 current, 8000 year-end 2026 (+4%) and 8700 at 12 months (+13%). GS EPS forecasts are $375 for 2026 (+36%), $415 for 2027 (+11%) and $460 for 2028 (+11%), versus bottom-up consensus of $367 and $425 for 2026 and 2027. Current NTM P/E is 19x.

Positioning and valuation gauges: the GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is 0.2, neither stretched nor light. The S&P 500 equal-weight forward P/E is 16x, the Nasdaq 100 22x and the Russell 2000 22x. Communication Services trades at the 4th percentile of its 10-year P/E range, while Health Care and Consumer Staples are at the 96th and 92nd.

Concentration is high: the 10 largest companies are 39% of S&P 500 market cap and 37% of earnings. YTD, crude oil (S&P GSCI) is the best-performing asset class shown, followed by Energy and Russell 1000 Value, while Bitcoin is the worst at -11%.
GS macro forecasts: 10-year US Treasury yield 5.0% now and 4.5% at 12 months, Brent $111 now and $75 at 12 months, COMEX gold $4,031 now and $5,140 at 12 months, USD/JPY 158 now and 150 at 12 months.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth tracking at 33% y/y with 60% of companies reported (reported results plus consensus for the remainder, excluding mega-cap tech other income). Q2 realized growth was also 33% on the same basis.

Median S&P 500 stock Q3 EPS growth tracking at 12% y/y versus 14% in Q2 and a 10-year median of 8%. Median stock sales growth decelerated modestly and median quarterly net profit margin expanded to a record.

Beat and miss frequency so far (reported, more than 1 standard deviation from consensus): 60% beat and 9% missed, versus a historical average of 50% beats and 13% misses. Equal-weighted: 60% positive, 9% negative, 31% in line, average earnings surprise 6%. Revenue: 46% positive, 12% negative, average surprise 2%.

Cap-weighted earnings surprises: Info Tech 93% positive and 0% negative, Communication Services 14% positive and 85% negative, Consumer Discretionary 16% positive and 3% negative, Energy 25% positive and 0% negative.
Q3 reported and consensus sector EPS growth: Energy 138%, Info Tech 67%, Comm Services 46%, Materials 39%, Industrials 23%. Info Tech sales growth is 43% and Energy sales growth 25%.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT) grew 54% y/y in Q3, above consensus estimates. Backlog growth slowed slightly versus Q2. Hyperscaler aggregate free cash flow was negative in Q3.

Consensus (estimate, not printed) hyperscaler capex is $806-808B for 2026 (+96%), about $1,163B for 2027 (+44%) and about $1,289B for 2028 (+11%) as of the current exhibit date. Consensus 2027 S&P 500 EPS is $425 bottom-up and $410 top-down strategist, versus GS at $415.
AI infrastructure EPS growth tracking at 80% y/y in Q3 (partly reported, partly consensus), with consensus pointing to about 40% by late 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated to 54% y/y in Q3 and beat consensus. Backlogs keep growing, and 2027 capex is still expected to rise to $1.2T, which supports AI infrastructure earnings growth of 80% in Q3.
tension_points.bear_case: GS sees capex growth peaking, hyperscaler free cash flow turned negative in Q3 and is expected to fall further in 2027, and consensus AI infrastructure EPS growth is expected to slow from 80% to about 40%. Crowded positioning left a high bar for share prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further decline in hyperscaler cloud backlog growth, or 2027 capex estimates being cut from the current $1.2T.

tension_points.bull_case: The median stock beating EPS outperformed by 152 bp and the S&P 500 ex. AI is up 5% since the start of the season, with cyclical sectors rewarded after beats.
tension_points.bear_case: TMT concentration still weighs on the index, which fell 3%. Rising energy prices are cutting margin estimates and revision breadth is positive in only half of sectors.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS says the outlook for energy prices and interest rates will determine whether the non-tech parts of the equity market can continue to rise.
